name: Familial Pseudohyperkalemia

criteria.description: Persistent elevation of serum potassium levels in vitro without clinical signs of hyperkalemia
Normal renal function and absence of conditions causing true hyperkalemia
Temperature-dependent leakage of potassium from erythrocytes demonstrated by in vitro testing
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of mutations in ABCB6 gene associated with the disorder

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of persistent elevated serum potassium without clinical hyperkalemia, normal renal function, and demonstration of temperature-dependent potassium leakage from erythrocytes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and laboratory-based; genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

laboratory: Elevated serum potassium in vitro with normal plasma potassium
Temperature-dependent potassium leakage from erythrocytes on storage
other: Absence of clinical hyperkalemia symptoms despite elevated serum potassium
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Clinical symptoms of hyperkalemia (muscle weakness, arrhythmias)
Evidence of hemolysis (elevated LDH, low haptoglobin)
Elevated serum potassium due to thrombocytosis

references: Alper SL. Familial pseudohyperkalemia: a benign inherited disorder of erythrocyte potassium transport. Blood Cells Mol Dis. 2007;39(2):124-7.
Kamel KS, et al. Familial pseudohyperkalemia: a review. Am J Kidney Dis. 1995;26(3):447-52.
